morphology_conclusions.central_frame: One native monolithic source with genuinely open beam windows and connected central round-ended lugs; fixed ownership agrees with S1 54/58/59. No restored split ties or red manufactured members required.
morphology_conclusions.moving_torso: Central ears appended to the existing fore/hind torso bodies; separate pin stack on E1/E2, no extra axis or command. Captures at 0/60/240 input phase visibly preserve fixed/moving ownership.
morphology_conclusions.plates: Separate fore/hind bodies and different surrounding motor mount structures retained. Long side slots, central slot and paired short curved openings/holes are plausible visual reconstructions. Mirroring a common motif is not proof the source had identical exact fore/hind patterns; hind capture partly occluded. No exact distinct rear pattern can be prescribed from the inspected source views.
morphology_conclusions.long_link: Broad rounded rectangular relief is a defensible morphology candidate. Source S1 56/59 supports longer relief family versus broad plain short bars. Through versus recessed depth, fork layering, edge chamfers and every named-link assignment remain ambiguous; no unsupported fork/bevel addition required.
morphology_conclusions.schematic: S1 51/54/64 red skeleton, rods and pegs are anatomy/kinematic illustrations, not manufactured-part evidence.

findings.title: Changed-material clearance is still a required candidate/package gate
findings.observation: AX0/AX1 three-pose transforms, native validity and neutral axis coincidence do not establish clearance of the added beams/lugs, clevis stems, pin stack or relieved link over motion.
findings.required_action: Lead to complete the already-running revision-specific clearance work on the repaired SHA, with exact changed pairs, contact exceptions, sample domain and failures recorded. Check lumbar versus both moving torso/clevis bodies, guide/C-shaft envelopes, motor/connector reservations, link layers and central retainers. Bind final exports to the accepted native artifact.

findings.title: Center-pin assembly order must account for the existing outer E journals
findings.observation: The center pin runs along the same Y line as the retained outer E journals. Their native axis records locate those journals outside the center stack; an insertion path from the side must pass their occupied axial positions. The source module only says before motors/cables. Closeups do not demonstrate a pin insertion or retainer tool path.
findings.required_action: Demonstrate center-pin insertion with the outer E journals removed/uninstalled; install the center pin and radial retainers before those journals, or document an alternate feasible sequence. Verify retainer installation/removal access and specify what must be removed for service. Do not claim in-place service access from the current static captures.

findings.title: Bearing outer-race retention and the axial/thrust path are not defined
findings.observation: A nominal Ø4 bearing is modeled in a Ø4.05 blind seat, with no specified fit or positive outer-race cap. Seat depth equals bearing width 1.2 mm. The moving OD3 washers are 0.2 mm clear of the lug and cannot establish a verified outer-race restraint or thrust path without the actual bearing ring geometry. Split-retainer spring material/installation strain and allowable thrust are also unknown.
findings.required_action: Select and inspect the actual bearing/retainer interfaces. Define housing and pin fits, outer-race retention, a race-specific thrust contact path, groove tolerances, installed endplay and retainer capacity. Update drawings/stack and geometry only as required by that resolved selection.

findings.title: The central support supplements an already redundant coaxial E support
findings.observation: The two moving clevis ears are integral to each torso while the central bearing pair is fixed to the lumbar; retained outer E supports act on that same rigid torso axis. Exact CAD coaxiality makes this consistent nominally, but does not accommodate printed bore position error or housing/pin deflection. The central pin has only 0.1 mm diametral clearance in the assumed Ø2 clevis bore.
findings.required_action: Declare which supports locate radially and axially, whether any support floats, and the coaxiality/reaming or alignment assembly process. Calculate permissible angular/position error and endplay before fabrication release. Avoid asserting a new kinematic DOF: this is a same-axis support/tolerance problem.

findings.title: Thin relief rails and lug/beam sections require a declared load/process check
findings.observation: The long B-C member has two 1.4 mm-wide rails at 1.2 mm thickness; nominal net rail area is 3.36 mm². Its Ø4.05 bores leave 0.975 mm radial ligament at a 6 mm-wide capsule end. The beam window roof/floor is 1.3 mm; opposed lug bearing seats leave a 0.8 mm central web. These are geometrically valid assumptions, not qualified printed or machined sections.
findings.required_action: Select material and fabrication orientation/process, then check reversal fatigue, pin bearing/tear-out, rail buckling/out-of-plane bending, beam torsion and lug root/seat splitting for declared loads. Include the Ø1.6 groove root in the pin load/retention check. Do not thicken or resize solely from image scaling.
